# **FG-02 \-- 009 \-- Manage Profile**

1. # **Use-Case Name**

   UC-009 — Manage Profile

   1. ## **Brief Description**

   An authenticated Customer views and updates their profile. Related avatar, verified email-change and initial-password subflows are consolidated here from the old Thành files while retaining their security boundaries.

   Functional group: FG-02 — Profile Management

   Actor(s): Customer (C)

   Priority: Core

2. # **Flow of Events**

   1. ## **Basic Flow**

   1\. The Customer opens My Profile. The System authenticates the session and loads the owned profile.

   2\. The System displays the Hza editable name, contact phone, gender/date of birth and read-only login email with separate password/email actions.

   3\. The Customer changes allowed profile fields and selects Save Changes.

   4\. The System validates supplied fields and updates only permitted fields, preserving omitted values.

   5\. The System returns the updated profile and displays the saved-profile confirmation.

   6\. The Customer may change an avatar through an eligible uploaded-image reference or open the separate verified-email subflow.

   7\. For email change, the Customer enters a new email; the System initiates verification while keeping the existing login email active.

   8\. Only after valid new-mailbox verification and required recent-authentication proof does the System replace the email and consume evidence.

   2. ## **Alternative Flows**

      1. ### *Input validation and business-rule alternatives*

   A1. At step 4, input is blank-only, invalid, too long or a supported username conflicts: reject the update and retain stored fields.

   A2. At step 4, general profile input attempts to change email/password or protected fields: reject it; use the separate protected actions.

   A3. At step 6, avatar replacement validates uploaded-image identity, eligibility and ownership before attaching it; a rejected reference preserves the prior avatar.

   A4. At step 6, conditional avatar removal clears only the profile reference and is harmless when already absent; it does not imply physical image deletion. Hza does not show a removal action.

   A5. At steps 7–8, new email equals the current email, is malformed/unavailable, or verification/recent-authentication proof is invalid: retain the existing email.

   A6. At step 7, resend invalidates earlier verification evidence; do not change the email merely on delivery or a button click.

      2. ### *Additional outcomes and service failures*

   A7. For a Google-only account without a local password, conditional initial-password setup requires reauthentication with the already linked Google identity, password validation and session revocation. If a password exists, use UC-006 instead.

   A8. At any owned-profile read/write, an expired session or cross-account identifier is rejected.

   A9. On service/save failure, retain the last confirmed profile and show retry; reconcile uncertain updates before claiming success.

3. # **Special Requirements**

   1. ## **Use-case quality and integrity constraints**

   • Hza separates contact phone from login email. Saving contact details must not silently change the login identity.

   • Earlier source field limits: display name 100 characters; username 50 with no @; profile phone 20 characters. Hza has no username input; expose only approved supported fields.

   • Earlier Backend profile reads include verification/account status, join date and local-password availability. Never return password plaintext/hash.

   • Email change discrepancy: Hza sends a link; the old source specifies six-digit codes valid ten minutes plus recent-authentication proof. Final verification/reauthentication UI and contract require resolution.

   • Initial-password source policy: at least eight characters, maximum 72 UTF-8 bytes, hashed storage and revocation of all sessions. This subflow has no Hza screen.

   • Preserve omitted fields; do not assume every optional field can be cleared. Avatar upload limits and deletion policy are not established.

4. # **Preconditions**

   1. ## **Conditions that must hold**

   • The Customer has a valid active account session.

   • The approved schema defines editable profile fields and protected identity-change operations.

5. # **Postconditions**

   1. ## **Success and failure states**

   Success:

   • Valid profile edits or separately verified identity changes are persisted for the owning Customer only.

   Failure:

   • Rejected changes preserve stored profile/login identity; private data are not exposed across accounts.

6. # **Extension Points**

   1. ## **Related use cases and scope**

   No named UML extension location is verified in the supplied model tab. Related use cases: UC-004 Verify Email (Guest registration only); UC-006 Change Password; UC-007 Login with Google; UC-010 Manage Shipping Addresses.

   Scope: Consolidates View/Update Profile, Update/Remove Picture, Change Email and Set Initial Password under canonical UC-009. Hza covers profile, saved confirmation and email-change request/check-mail screens; avatar removal and initial-password UI remain gaps.

   Sources: Vision v1.4; shared PA3 Use-Case Model; Hza.zip static exports; earlier Thành specifications dated 11 November 2026\. Prior Backend statements have not been revalidated against repository code in this revision.
